slides.title: Your first website, built by AI
slides.text: A web page isn't a mysterious program: it's a text file with markup inside it. The language of that markup is called HTML (the language web pages are written in). You can open the file with Windows Notepad and read it, even if you don't understand half of it. The browser (the program you use to get on the internet: Chrome, Safari, Edge) reads that text and paints it. Where it finds a heading marker it draws a big…
items: Lucía's website ended up being a file called index.html, 380 lines and 21 KB, less than a phone photo. Inside were her three cakes with their prices (€35, €60, and from €95), her WhatsApp, her hours, and her two colors.

slides.title: Practice: Write your data sheet before opening the AI
slides.text: Almost everything that's going to go wrong goes wrong here, so give it five real minutes. Write these nine lines with your real details, not approximate ones: 1) the exact name, spelled the way you want it read; 2) what you do, in one sentence; 3) your city; 4) three things you sell or do, each with its price in dollars; 5) your phone or WhatsApp with all the digits; 6) your email; 7) your hours or your real policy,…
items: In Windows Notepad, in your phone's Notes app, or on paper. Still outside the AI.
A notes.txt file with nine lines, three prices in dollars, and a phone number with all its digits. If reading it back you can't say what the single action from point 9 is, it's not finished yet.

slides.title: Asking for changes without breaking what already works
slides.text: When you ask for a change to something it already built you, it doesn't pick up a scalpel. It rewrites the whole chunk from what it has in front of it at that moment. Today's tools try to touch only the affected part, but they decide where that part starts and ends, and when they get the boundary wrong they take out whatever was next to it. What keeps what already worked standing isn't that the AI remembers it…
items: Álvaro asked for the page to be "more modern." It came back with a different font, more breathing room, new colors, and the contact section rewritten from top to bottom. In that rewrite, the link that opened WhatsApp with his number…

slides.text: Before asking for any change, get yourself a copy. Paste the message below, wait for the code block, and click the "Copy" button that appears at the top right of the block. Create a folder on your desktop called "versions" and inside it an empty text file (on Windows: right-click on the folder, "New" and "Text Document"; on Mac: TextEdit, then the "Format" menu and "Make Plain Text," because otherwise it saves it…
items: In the Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini app, in the chat where you have something that already works

A long code block with a "Copy" button above it and, below it, a short sentence like "Booking page with calendar, prices, and WhatsApp button." On your desktop, a file that opens in the browser when you double-click it and looks the same…

slides.title: When something breaks and you don't understand the error
slides.text: You ask Claude or ChatGPT for a page. It writes the code (the instructions the computer reads and executes) and hands it to you. That's where its involvement ends. What runs that code is your browser, on your computer, with your files, your connection, and your version of Windows. Of all that, the AI receives nothing: no image, no notice, no beep. It's the doubt everyone has the first time: if it wrote it, how…
items: Nacho wrote "the page won't load." Claude rewrote the whole file. It still wouldn't load. Nacho wrote "still the same" and Claude rewrote it again, now with a different structure. Three rounds and forty minutes later, the cause was the…

slides.title: Practice: Open the browser console and stop fearing it
slides.text: Open a page you use every day. Press the F12 key, up at the top right of the keyboard. On Mac, press Cmd + Alt + J. If nothing happens, right-click any empty spot on the page and choose "Inspect" from the menu that appears. The screen splits in two and in the new half you'll see a row of tabs: Elements, Console, Sources, Network... Click "Console." Now, with the panel already open, reload the page with F5 and watch…
items: In your browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari), with any page open

A panel taking up half the bottom or right side of the window. You'll see the word Console highlighted and, below it, lines of text. On a large site you'll see yellow warnings and probably some red errors. That's normal: the world's most…

slides.title: Claude Code: when you want to move a lot faster
slides.text: In the app, Claude only sees what you paste to it and only gives you back text that you have to paste yourself. That back-and-forth is the bottleneck. The AI doesn't think slowly: you're the one acting as messenger between it and your files. Claude Code is that same Claude placed inside a folder on your computer. It opens the files itself, reads them all, edits them, and runs things. Here's a question that's bound…
items: Diego wanted to change the contact phone number on his site, which appeared in fourteen files. By hand, searching and pasting from the chat: twenty-two minutes, and he missed one. With Claude Code: forty seconds, and all fourteen done.

slides.title: Practice: Decide whether it's your turn or not yet
slides.text: Before installing absolutely anything. Open a new chat and paste the message below, filling in the blanks with the truth, not with what you'd like it to be. To count the files, open your project folder in the file explorer and count them by eye. If the answer you get is "not yet," you've just saved yourself an entire weekend of installations.

A verdict in the first line, no beating around the bush. With fewer than five files and nothing working yet, "not yet" is normal, and that's a good result. With twelve files and fifteen copy-pastes a session it'll tell you yes, and you'll…

slides.title: Reviewing what AI writes without knowing how to code
slides.text: You're never going to read that code and you don't need to. What you do need to do is exactly what anyone hiring a contractor does. Know which rooms they went into. Turn on the tap to see if water comes out. And have it in writing what was done. Three questions cover almost everything: what have you touched, does what worked before still work, and what aren't you telling me. None of the three requires understanding…
items: Nuria is a physical therapist in Salamanca and has a website for her patients to book appointments. She asked to change a button's green. The AI changed the button and, "while it was at it," unified the colors across the whole project: 19…

slides.title: Practice: Duplicate the folder before asking for anything at all
slides.text: Find your project folder. Click it once to select it, press Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on Mac), and then Ctrl+V (Cmd+V) in that same spot. A copy will appear named with "- copy" at the end. Right-click the copy and choose "Rename." Give it the original name plus today's date and what you're about to do: for example "gijoncoffee-2026-08-19-before-coupons." Don't move it elsewhere, leave it right next to the original. If your…
items: In your computer's file explorer: on Windows the yellow folder in the taskbar; on Mac Finder, the blue face in the Dock

Two folders side by side: the working one with its usual name and the copy with the date. Open it and check it has the same content as the original, not an empty folder. If your project is over 1 GB, it's probably mostly the node_modules…

slides.title: What would prevent your project from being handed off?
slides.text: Use one case you actually observed. Name the evidence, the risk and the next check. There is no automatically correct option for this open question.

Unreliable repeated event
